label: Butter lamp
note: Burns clarified butter, in Tibetan Buddhism clarified yak butter, as fuel; now often vegetable oil.

about.text: A lamp that burns butter, in Tibetan Buddhism clarified yak butter, now often vegetable oil.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Not a food step: the clarified butter is not processed further, it is burned as lamp fuel, so the arrow adds nothing to clarified butter itself. Pilgrims supply lamp oil as an offering and monks tend the lamps.

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

facts.v: Clarified yak butter, burned as is
Often vegetable oil or vanaspati ghee (Wikipedia marks this claim as needing a citation)
